abstract:
|
  Round 4 on issue #65's citation-resolver gate: an owner-ruled remedy following the round-3 review's REJECT-ESCALATED verdict, which found the CODE excellent (all six new tests proven non-vacuous under the reviewer's own fault injections) but named the real defect as the instrument itself - a roughly 360-line hand-written measurement narrative living in the one file exempt from every mechanical check this repo has, which had produced a false claim in all three prior rounds despite each round's fixes being individually correct. The owner concurred with Option A (amputate) rather than continuing to iterate on prose.

  This round is architecturally different from rounds 1-3: it deletes rather than corrects. The header was cut to its operational minimum - three short paragraphs stating what binds, what does not, and the scope/exemption mechanics, plus one pointer sentence directing all history and calibration evidence to the three landed review verdicts rather than restating any of it in prose. Every body comment across the file's functions and test blocks was swept the same way, removing round-history and finding-ID labels while keeping the operational content (what the code does, what the test proves) intact. The one comment the coordinator named explicitly - an overclaim that a single fixture "moved a 3-for-3 claim from prose to a pin" when it in fact pinned one of three legs - was deleted along with the Describe block's own overclaiming name, replaced with a name stating exactly what the fixture demonstrates.

  Critically, zero test logic was touched: the same 28 real assertions and 4 informational skips that passed before the amputation pass identically after it, verified by direct comparison rather than assumed. The diff is accordingly deletion-dominant (108 insertions against 556 deletions in the single file touched), and a targeted self-check confirms the new header carries no calibration numbers - every remaining digit is either a pointer (the issue number, the verdict filenames) or the one threshold the ruling itself required to be stated (the content-anchor's bind trigger).

  All suites re-confirmed green at the new HEAD: scripts/tests 223/0/4-skipped/227 (identical split to round 3), scripts/probes 24/24, CodeCitationPolicy.Tests.ps1 in isolation 13/13. Go, Node, and probe-yard-snapshot.mjs were not re-run since only test-file prose changed this round, stated plainly per the brief.
